t: Caodaists worship one God, Cao Đài, and hold that all religions come from the same source; they believe that God has revealed his will in three eras and that the third and final revelation is given through the Cao Đài faith.
The religion began in 1925 in Saigon with a group of colonial clerks who held séances, and was officially established at Tây Ninh in 1926; by 1940 it had gathered over a million members.
Its church is organised in a hierarchy with a Pope, Cardinals, Bishops and Priests, and its clergy wear yellow, azure or red for the Buddhist, Taoist and Confucianist branches.
dyk: Caodaists hold that Victor Hugo, Sun Yat-sen and Trạng Trình, the Vietnamese Nostradamus, are the three main prophets of the Cao Đài pantheon, as a plaque at the entrance of the Tây Ninh Temple shows.
ev: Cao Quỳnh Cư, Cao Hoài Sang, Lê Văn Trung and Phạm Công Tắc found a Spiritualist club named AĂÂ in Saigon to practise mediumship
Ngô Văn Chiêu signs the Declaration of the Founding of the Cao Đài Religion on 7 October, and the religion is officially established at Tây Ninh
Lê Văn Trung, the first and only officially ordained Pope of the Tây Ninh Holy See, dies and Phạm Công Tắc takes over his role
The religion has gathered over a million members, between a fifth and a quarter of the population of Cochinchina
Phạm Công Tắc and other Caodaist leaders are arrested and jailed in French penal colonies in Madagascar, where they stay until 1946
After the fall of Saigon the incoming communist government bans the practice of Caodaism
Caodaism is granted legal recognition and unrestricted practice once again

f.origin: Saigon, Southern Vietnam, in 1925, as a Spiritualist club; officially established in the city of Tây Ninh in 1926.
f.founder: Cao Quỳnh Cư, Cao Hoài Sang, Lê Văn Trung and Phạm Công Tắc, clerks in the colonial government who founded the Spiritualist club in 1925; Ngô Văn Chiêu, revered as the first disciple of the Đức Cao Đài, signed the declaration of founding on 7 October 1926.
f.scriptures: Several sets of scriptures; those of the Tây Ninh Holy See include Kinh Thiên Đạo Và Thế Đạo (Prayers of the Heavenly and the Earthly Way), Pháp Chánh Truyền (the Religious Constitution), Tân Luật (the Canonical Codes) and Con Đường Thiêng Liêng Hằng Sống (Divine Path to Eternal Life).
f.followers: Estimates vary: government figures give 4.4 million affiliated to the Tây Ninh Holy See and up to 6 million with other branches; the United Nations estimated about 2.5 million in Vietnam in January 2015; tens of thousands live abroad, mainly in North America, Cambodia, Europe and Australia.
